question.text: Which of the following statements about Fund Administrators for Indian AIFs is MOST accurate?

answer.text: Fund Administrator is a SEBI-regulated function requiring separate registration.
Only the Trustee is allowed to act as the Fund Administrator.
Fund Administrator must be a Chartered Accountant firm only.
Fund administration is NOT a regulated function in India and can be performed by custodians, third-party vendors, or in-house.

explanation.text: The Logic: Unlike in several developed markets, fund administration / fund accounting is NOT a regulated function in India. The role can be performed by the custodian (which typically offers administration alongside custody), a specialised third-party vendor, or kept in-house — particularly if investor count is low or NAV computation is infrequent. Many foreign funds use India-based fund administrators for cost efficiency. The Trap: Option A invents a registration regime. Option B wrongly ring-fences the role to the trustee. Option C invents a CA-only restriction. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C, XIX-D test the same unregulated-status rule. XXI-B (PM) has a different regulated-administration regime via CCIL.
